transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-12
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Oliver Grant (SummitEdge Partnerships); Nina Park (SummitEdge Sales Ops); Samir Desai (SummitEdge Solutions); Lena Ortiz (SummitEdge AE)

Summary (auto): co-sell pipeline review, alignment on top deals, docs to share, schedule technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intros for anyone new — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ravi, our SE.
[00:10] Oliver Grant: Hey all, Oliver here, partnerships at SummitEdge. Nina and Samir and Lena are also on.
[00:18] Nina Park: Hi, yeah thanks, we got the agenda.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: Great, quick agenda — pipeline overview from Samir, then deal by deal qualification for co-sell, technical flags, and next steps.
[00:30] Samir Desai: Cool, I'll kick it off. We have seven deals in the near-term co-sell funnel. Top three are: DeltaHealth (healthcare payer), OrionRetail (e-commerce), and MeridianBank (finserv). The rest are smaller pilots.
[00:47] Lena Ortiz: For DeltaHealth, procurement asked about VPC/private deployment and SOC2, do you have a quick answer?
[00:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we do. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; we have SOC 2 and can do KMS integrations. I'll send our compliance pack after.
[01:05] Oliver Grant: Perfect. On OrionRetail they're worried about latency at 99th percentile. How have you seen lat p99 on dedicated vs hosted?
[01:14] Ravi Patel: Good question — typical p99 for dedicated with our optimized runtime is in the 120–200 ms range for single-turn generation at 512 tokens, depends a lot on batch size and model family. Hosted can be slightly higher but we have options to route to dedicated for SLAs.
[01:30] Nina Park: Is that on A100 or the newer chips?
[01:34] Ravi Patel: Mostly A100 and H100 in our Dedicated pools; for H100 you can see lower median but p99 still workload dependent. Also, kv-cache and prefix caching matter a lot for chat workloads — sometimes people confuse KV cache with KMS, so just a note, sorry for the jargon.
[01:55] Samir Desai: For MeridianBank — they're big on encryption and audit trails. Can you support customer-managed keys and long-term audit logs?
[02:04] Maya Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and detailed audit logs; for full compliance we recommend Private deployment. We'll attach audit sample logs in the doc pack.
[02:18] Oliver Grant: Awesome. Okay deal-by-deal — Samir, can you run through the top three with state and ask?
[02:26] Samir Desai: Sure. DeltaHealth — currently on evaluation with ML infra team; they'd need a POC for PHI-safe inference, timeline end of Q4; ask: demo + security docs + pilot proposal. OrionRetail — pilot with 10k daily users, need latency guarantees and pricing; ask: joint proposal and co-marketing. MeridianBank — procurement wants a closed-network deployment and an SLA; ask: dedicated footprint and SSO/SAML integration.
[02:54] Maya Chen: Good. For DeltaHealth, we should propose Redwood Private or a very locked-down Dedicated instance and propose an initial pilot scope focusing on redaction and data residency. I'll volunteer to draft the pilot scope.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: For OrionRetail, what pricing model works for co-sell — usage-based or seat/commit?
[03:17] Maya Chen: Usually for co-sell we propose reserved capacity for predictable unit economics, coupled with overage usage-based. But we can model both; I'll include a sample pricing sheet.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: And on the latency piece, we can run a pareto test — pick representative prompts, run them on dedicated H100 profile and share p50/p90/p99 numbers.
[03:40] Oliver Grant: That'd help. Who owns the benchmarking?
[03:44] Ravi Patel: I can run it with Samir's team if they can share the prompt set and typical sequence lengths.
[03:50] Samir Desai: We can share a scrubbed prompt set. I'll get that to you.
[03:54] Nina Park: A question — when a deal is co-sell ready, what are the go-to-market assets you provide? Playbook, joint case study, demand gen?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a co-sell playbook, joint pitch deck, joint PR templates, and a partner portal with enablement. We'll share a condensed playbook PDF after the call.
[04:12] Oliver Grant: Any conflicts with other partners or competitor references we should be aware of?
[04:17] Maya Chen: Not on our side; we've had some overlap with big clouds like AWS Bedrock, but our angle is performance/cost controls and seamless private options.
[04:27] Samir Desai: Ok good. Next, the deal qualification rubric — quick go/no-go flags: data residency, tech fit, budget/time-to-buy.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: On tech fit: if they need on-prem, we can support but there is a lead time for packaging; if they need specialized quantization we have guidance but there can be model quality tradeoffs.
[04:50] Lena Ortiz: Can you quantify lead time for Private deployment?
[04:54] Maya Chen: Typical on-prem/private engagements take 6–10 weeks from kickoff depending on infra readiness; Dedicated reservation can be faster if they accept cloud-hosted dedicated pools.
[05:06] Nina Park: That's useful. For DeltaHealth timeline end of Q4 — might be tight for on-prem then.
[05:12] Samir Desai: Noted. We'll surface that to the customer.
[05:15] Maya Chen: If needed, we can propose a hybrid — start hosted with strict controls and move to Private for production.
[05:22] Oliver Grant: Let's move into the pipeline spreadsheet — Nina, any updates from your side on open opportunities?
[05:28] Nina Park: Yes, added win probs and expected close dates; I flagged three as co-sell-ready: OrionRetail (60%), DeltaHealth (40%), MeridianBank (30%). Others are earlier.
[05:38] Maya Chen: Great. For the co-sell-ready ones, we'll prioritize joint outreach — recommended owners: Maya for OrionRetail, Oliver to coordinate joint messaging, Samir to manage tech validation.
[05:52] Ravi Patel: Quick technical note on OrionRetail — their frontend uses longchat sessions with 2–3k tokens typical; recommend we test larger context windows and see memory/latency impact.
[06:04] Samir Desai: We'll include sample session traces.
[06:08] Oliver Grant: On MeridianBank, procurement asked about indemnity and data flow diagrams. Do you have a standard SOW addendum?
[06:16] Maya Chen: We have standard SOW templates and can produce a data flow diagram; legal might need a couple back-and-forths. I'll loop in our legal contacts if it moves forward.
[06:26] Lena Ortiz: Any blockers you see for these deals?
[06:29] Ravi Patel: Mostly around security for DeltaHealth and procurement terms for MeridianBank; OrionRetail is mostly performance & pricing.
[06:36] Nina Park: Okay. For action items, can we capture owners and dates?
[06:41] Maya Chen: Yes — I'll send the pricing and playbook by tomorrow, Samir to share the scrubbed prompts and pipeline CSV by Friday, and Ravi will schedule a perf run and technical deep dive with SummitEdge engineering next week.
[06:56] Samir Desai: Note — a potential new logo, NovaRetail, might slot into Q1 2026 if we can do a quick pilot.
[07:04] Maya Chen: Good to track. Any competitive intel — Samir, you mentioned AWS Bedrock earlier?
[07:09] Samir Desai: They asked about using Bedrock for a fully managed stack; concerns are cost at scale and model flavor availability.
[07:17] Ravi Patel: We also compete with Vertex and Anthropic in certain deals; worth noting for messaging.
[07:24] Oliver Grant: Ok, let's run a quick run-of-show for the technical deep dive — Ravi, what do you need from SummitEdge eng?
[07:29] Ravi Patel: Access to scrubbed prompt sets, expected qps, token distribution, and any security constraints (e.g., IP allowlist, SSO flow). Ideally an engineer from their infra team on the call.
[07:41] Lena Ortiz: I'll coordinate to get an infra engineer on the slot.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Also share any test data or sanitized dataset for throughput testing.
[07:49] Samir Desai: We'll package that.
[07:52] Maya Chen: Good. A practical ask — can SummitEdge prioritize the top three deals and indicate which ones they want Redwood to lead on joint outreach?
[07:59] Nina Park: Yes — we'll mark OrionRetail and DeltaHealth as joint-owned and MeridianBank as partner-led for now.
[08:07] Maya Chen: Thanks. Any other questions?
[08:09] Oliver Grant: One more — what's the co-sell commission split typically?
[08:12] Maya Chen: That varies by partner program and deal; we'll propose a standard split in the playbook, and we can adjust per-deal if needed.
[08:20] Samir Desai: Okay.
[08:22] Maya Chen: Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps — Maya to send playbook + pricing by 2025-09-13, Samir to share pipeline CSV and scrubbed prompts by 2025-09-19, Ravi to run perf tests and schedule deep dive week of 2025-09-22. SummitEdge to confirm owners on pipeline.
[08:43] Oliver Grant: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:46] Nina Park: Thanks.
[08:47] Samir Desai: Thanks all.
[08:49] Maya Chen: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes (auto): References to SOC2, KMS, KV cache, H100/A100, VPC, private deployment, SSO/SAML, p99 latency, reserved capacity, co-sell playbook, joint pricing.

End of transcript.
